<description>
A corrupt `blocks/index` can stop the node at startup. A last block file number of -1 makes it read before the start of a vector. A very large one makes it allocate and read that many file infos. A block without a parent, or with a parent at the wrong height, hits the assert in `CBlockIndex::GetAncestor`.

I reject these entries on load, so init reports the usual database error and suggests `-reindex`. A last file without stored info is still accepted when the file before it has info, because running out of disk space while opening a new file leaves that state. The new unit tests fail on master, and the reindex, pruning and assumeutxo functional tests pass. #32427 would replace this database and derive the last file number from its entries.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
93bafbdfdc blockstorage: validate last file and parent links

A last block file number of -1 in blocks/index makes the node read
before the start of a vector. A very large one makes it allocate and
read that many file infos. A block without a parent, or with a parent at
the wrong height, hits the assert in CBlockIndex::GetAncestor.

I reject a negative number. I also reject a last file number when
neither that file nor the one before it has stored file info. The file
before is enough because the node can claim a new file and run out of
disk space before writing to it. Every block above genesis must have a
parent at the previous height. Loading then fails with an error, and the
node asks for -reindex. Unit tests cover each case.
</commits>
